statement: The supplied target states a componentwise backward-error representation for the particular reduction defined here: for positive input count n, arbitrary real coordinate arrays, nonnegative u, active-addition errors bounded in absolute value by u, and depth(n) u<1, its output equals an exact sum of perturbed inputs with componentwise perturbation at most gamma(depth(n),u) times the absolute input. At each stage the construction pairs positions separated by the next stage size, multiplies each paired sum by 1+δ, copies unpaired positions unchanged, and discards inactive positions by setting them to zero. It returns position 0 after the ceiling base-2 logarithm of n stages. Coefficients follow that same recurrence from indicator inputs; backwardPerturbation uses final coefficients minus one times each input. The theorem is existential and does not explicitly designate that constructed perturbation as its witness.

targets.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.parallel_binary_tree_reduction
targets.statement: For every type ι at any universe level and every n ∈ ℕ with 0<n, for every x : Fin n → (ι → ℝ), every real u with 0≤u, and every δ : ℕ → ℕ → ι → ℝ satisfying LocalRoundingModel(n,u,δ), assume also (d : ℝ)u<1, where d=depth(n). Then there exists Δx : Fin n → (ι → ℝ) such that computed(x,δ)=∑_{i∈Fin n}(x(i)+Δx(i)) as functions ι → ℝ, and for every i ∈ Fin n and c ∈ ι, |Δx(i,c)|≤gamma(d,u)|x(i,c)|=((d : ℝ)u/(1−(d : ℝ)u))|x(i,c)|. Here Fin n is {0,…,n−1}; addition and sums of functions are pointwise. Equivalently, for every c ∈ ι, stage(x,δ,d,0,c)=∑_{i=0}^{n−1}(x(i,c)+Δx(i,c)). LocalRoundingModel means precisely the active-pair bounds given in its construction description. This theorem concerns the specified offset-pairing recurrence, evaluated at stage d and position 0. Its existential conclusion does not explicitly identify Δx with the separately constructed backwardPerturbation.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.depth
constructions.description: For n ∈ ℕ, depth(n) = Nat.clog(2,n), the natural ceiling logarithm base 2. It is 0 for n = 0; for n > 0 it is the least d ∈ ℕ with n ≤ 2^d. In particular depth(1) = 0. This is the stage used for the final output and coefficients and the factor in the target bound.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.stageSize
constructions.description: For all n,ℓ ∈ ℕ, s_ℓ = stageSize(n,ℓ) = (n+2^ℓ−1) div 2^ℓ = ceil(n/2^ℓ). Subtraction is truncated natural subtraction and div is natural integer division. Since 2^ℓ ≥ 1 the subtraction does not truncate here. In particular s_0 = n and stageSize(0,ℓ) = 0. These sizes determine the active positions and pairing offsets.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.gamma
constructions.description: For every k ∈ ℕ and u ∈ ℝ, gamma(k,u) = ((k : ℝ)u)/(1−(k : ℝ)u). This definition has no hypotheses: Lean real division is total, with a zero denominator giving zero. In the target, k = depth(n), 0 ≤ u and k u < 1, so the denominator is positive.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.stage
constructions.description: For an arbitrary type ι, n ∈ ℕ, x : Fin n → ι → ℝ and δ : ℕ → ℕ → ι → ℝ, define S_ℓ(k,c) = stage(x,δ,ℓ,k,c) for every ℓ,k ∈ ℕ and c ∈ ι. Set S_0(k,c) = x(⟨k,k<n⟩,c) if k<n and 0 otherwise. At each ℓ let m = stageSize(n,ℓ+1), s = stageSize(n,ℓ). For k ≥ m set S_{ℓ+1}(k,c)=0. For k<m and k+m<s set S_{ℓ+1}(k,c)=(S_ℓ(k,c)+S_ℓ(k+m,c))(1+δ(ℓ,k,c)). For k<m and k+m≥s set S_{ℓ+1}(k,c)=S_ℓ(k,c). Thus it pairs positions k and k+m of the preceding stage, where m is the next size; it does not pair consecutive indices 2k and 2k+1. An unpaired entry is copied with no error factor. The operations are exact real operations with supplied multiplicative factors. The definition specifies no machine arithmetic, parallel execution schedule, or probabilistic mechanism. It is defined for all stages, even beyond depth(n), without rounding hypotheses.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.computed
constructions.description: For every type ι, n ∈ ℕ, x : Fin n → ι → ℝ and δ : ℕ → ℕ → ι → ℝ, computed(x,δ) is the function c ↦ stage(x,δ,depth(n),0,c). For n>0 the active size at this stage is one. For n=0 this definition returns the zero function, although the target excludes n=0. For n=1 it returns the sole input unchanged.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.LocalRoundingModel
constructions.description: For every type ι, n ∈ ℕ, u ∈ ℝ and δ : ℕ → ℕ → ι → ℝ, LocalRoundingModel(n,u,δ) means: for every ℓ ∈ ℕ with ℓ<depth(n), every k ∈ ℕ with k<stageSize(n,ℓ+1) and k+stageSize(n,ℓ+1)<stageSize(n,ℓ), and every c ∈ ι, |δ(ℓ,k,c)|≤u. It bounds exactly active paired additions used before the final output stage. It places no restrictions on unused entries, unpaired positions, or stages at or beyond depth(n). It does not itself assume u≥0 and is vacuous if there are no active pairs.

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.coefficient
constructions.description: For every type ι, n ∈ ℕ and δ : ℕ → ℕ → ι → ℝ, define A_ℓ(k,i,c)=coefficient(δ,ℓ,k,i,c), for ℓ,k ∈ ℕ, i ∈ Fin n and c ∈ ι. Set A_0(k,i,c)=1 when k equals the natural value of i, and 0 otherwise. For every ℓ put m=stageSize(n,ℓ+1), s=stageSize(n,ℓ). If k≥m set A_{ℓ+1}(k,i,c)=0. If k<m and k+m<s set A_{ℓ+1}(k,i,c)=(A_ℓ(k,i,c)+A_ℓ(k+m,i,c))(1+δ(ℓ,k,c)). If k<m and k+m≥s set A_{ℓ+1}(k,i,c)=A_ℓ(k,i,c). This is the same recurrence applied to the indicator input for i; it does not depend on x. Consequently the definitions yield S_ℓ(k,c)=∑_{i∈Fin n} A_ℓ(k,i,c)x(i,c). Final coefficients are A_depth(n)(0,i,c).

constructions.name: Research.BinaryTreeReduction.backwardPerturbation
constructions.description: For every type ι, n ∈ ℕ, x : Fin n → ι → ℝ, δ : ℕ → ℕ → ι → ℝ, i ∈ Fin n and c ∈ ι, backwardPerturbation(x,δ,i,c)=x(i,c)(coefficient(δ,depth(n),0,i,c)−1). Thus x(i,c)+backwardPerturbation(x,δ,i,c)=x(i,c)coefficient(δ,depth(n),0,i,c). The coefficient expansion of stage connects this specific perturbation to computed: its perturbed inputs sum exactly to computed. The definition imposes no rounding or smallness hypotheses. The target asserts existence of a bounded perturbation but does not explicitly name backwardPerturbation as its witness.

assumptions: The coordinate index ι is any type at any universe level; neither finiteness nor inhabitance is required. All coordinate quantifiers range over every c ∈ ι.
The target quantifies over all n ∈ ℕ subject to 0<n. Input indices range over Fin n={0,…,n−1}.
The input x : Fin n → ι → ℝ is arbitrary; there is no sign, magnitude, or nonzero-entry assumption.

The error array δ : ℕ → ℕ → ι → ℝ satisfies |δ(ℓ,k,c)|≤u whenever ℓ<depth(n), k<stageSize(n,ℓ+1), and k+stageSize(n,ℓ+1)<stageSize(n,ℓ), for every coordinate c. No restrictions are imposed on other error entries.
The additional hypothesis is (depth(n) : ℝ)u<1. There is no separate assumption u<1; when n=1 its depth is zero.

The constructions are defined without the target hypotheses for all natural n and all real arrays and parameters in their domains. Stage indices, sizes and comparisons use natural numbers; data values and factors use real arithmetic.
